subject: Computing
title: Stage 1 Computing Readiness Check
description: A short, friendly check of tapping and typing, following steps in order and staying safe, so we can find your perfect starting point.
attemptsAllowed: Unlimited — this exam finds your starting point; it is never a fail
feedbackMode: Immediate child-friendly feedback with a placement report

ready.label: Ready for Stage 1
ready.message: Brilliant work! You can tap, type, follow steps and stay safe. Stage 1, here you come.

readyWithReview.label: Ready — with a little review
readyWithReview.message: You are ready to start Stage 1. Warm up first with the review lessons below.

notReady.label: Let's build strong roots first
notReady.message: Let's practise tapping, clicking and following steps before Stage 1. A grown-up or teacher can sit with you and explore a computer or tablet together.

recommendation.label: Stage 1 Computing, Unit 1 with a grown-up

sections.title: Using a device
sections.description: Do you know how to tap a screen, use a mouse and a keyboard, and look after a device?

sections.title: Following steps
sections.description: Can you follow simple steps in the right order, one at a time?

sections.title: Staying safe
sections.description: Do you know when to ask a grown-up for help with screens and secrets?

questions.question: Layla wants to open a picture on a tablet. What should she do with her finger?
questions.options: wave at the tablet from far away | tap the picture gently | shake the tablet up and down | hit the screen very hard
questions.explanation: A gentle tap with one finger tells the tablet what you want. Screens like soft, careful touches.

questions.question: Omar wants to type the letters of his name on a computer. Which part does he press?
questions.options: the cable | the keyboard | the mouse | the speaker
questions.explanation: The keyboard is full of letter buttons called keys. Pressing them makes letters appear on the screen.

questions.question: Which part of a computer shows you the pictures and words?
questions.options: the plug | the screen | the mouse | the keyboard
questions.explanation: The screen is like a window — it shows you all the pictures, words and games.

questions.question: Amina slides the mouse and a little arrow moves on the screen. What is that little arrow called?
questions.options: a bird | a kite | a pencil | the pointer
questions.explanation: The little arrow is called the pointer. When you move the mouse, the pointer moves too — they are a team!

questions.question: Yusuf has finished his game. What is the careful way to treat the tablet?
questions.options: drop it on the floor | take it into the bath | leave it out in the rain | put it away gently with clean, dry hands
questions.correctAnswer: put it away gently with clean, dry hands
questions.explanation: Tablets and computers are delicate. Clean, dry hands and a gentle touch keep them working for a long time.

questions.question: To wash your hands you follow steps: turn on the tap, rub with soap, dry your hands. What do you do first?
questions.options: put on your shoes | turn on the tap | rub with soap | dry your hands
questions.explanation: Steps work best in order. First the tap goes on, then the soap, and drying comes last.

questions.question: Sara makes toast with three steps: put the bread in the toaster, wait for it to pop, spread the butter. What does she do after the toast pops?
questions.options: brush her teeth | turn off the lights | put in more bread | spread the butter
questions.explanation: After the toast pops, the next step is spreading the butter. Doing steps in order gets the job done right.

questions.question: A toy robot listens to these steps: forward, forward, turn. Which step does the robot do first?
questions.explanation: The robot always starts with the first step on the list — forward! It follows the steps one at a time, in order.

questions.question: Bilan draws a house with two steps: first draw a big square, then draw a roof on top. Which does he draw first?
questions.options: the roof | the front door | the big square | a tree
questions.explanation: First comes the square, because the roof needs a house to sit on. Steps in the right order make the drawing work.

questions.question: A game asks Hodan to type her name and where she lives. What should she do?
questions.options: type it in quickly | ask a friend to type it for her | tell the game the name of her school | stop and ask a grown-up first
questions.correctAnswer: stop and ask a grown-up first
questions.explanation: Your name and where you live are private. Always stop and ask a grown-up before telling a game or website anything about you.

questions.question: Adam sees something on the screen that makes him feel scared or upset. What should he do?
questions.options: hide the tablet under his bed | tell a grown-up he trusts | keep it a secret | watch it again and again
questions.explanation: If a screen ever makes you feel scared or upset, telling a grown-up you trust is always the right thing to do. You will never be in trouble for telling.

questions.question: A password is like a secret key for the tablet. Who is it okay to share it with?
questions.options: anyone who says please | only your own grown-ups at home | everyone in the playground | a stranger who asks online
questions.correctAnswer: only your own grown-ups at home
questions.explanation: A password is a special secret. Only your own grown-ups at home should know it — it keeps your things safe.
